pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Anti-N-Methyl-D-Aspartate (Anti-NMDA) Receptor Encephalitis THE SMOKING GUN: Characteristic extreme delta brush pattern on EEG paired with an occult pelvic ultrasound revealing a mature ovarian teratoma (dermoid cyst) PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis is a severe autoimmune disorder characterized by IgG antibodies targeted directly against the extracellular GluN1 subunit of the NMDA receptor in the central nervous system. In approximately 50% of young female presentations, the underlying driver is a mature ovarian teratoma containing ectopic, dysplastic neural elements. The host immune system recognizes these neoplastic neural antigens as foreign, mounting an antibody response that cross-reacts with endogenous neuronal NMDA receptors in the hippocampus, forebrain, and brainstem. Binding of these autoantibodies induces cross-linking and selective internalization (downregulation) of surface NMDA receptors without causing complement-mediated structural cell lysis. This produces a state of neuronal hypo-function, disrupting inhibitory GABAergic pathways and leading to unconstrained dopaminergic and glutamatergic surges. The resulting clinical cascade manifests sequentially as psychiatric prodrome, movement disorders/dyskinesias, autonomic instability, and hypoventilation. Treatment requires tumor resection alongside aggressive immunotherapy (plasma exchange, IVIG, and rituximab/cyclophosphamide).
